arxiv-2109-10156.title: A Variability Fault Localization Approach for Software Product Lines
arxiv-2109-10156.creator: Thu-Trang Nguyen, Kien-Tuan Ngo, Son Nguyen, and Hieu Dinh Vo
arxiv-2109-10156.description: Abstract Software fault localization is one of the most expensive, tedious, and time-consuming activities in program debugging. This activity becomes even much more challenging in Software Product Line (SPL) systems due to variability of failures. These unexpected behaviors are induced by variability faults which can only be exposed under some combinations of system features.

arxiv-2202-12617.title: Algorithmic Computability and Approximability of Capacity-Achieving Input Distributions
arxiv-2202-12617.creator: Holger Boche, Rafael F. Schaefer, H. Vincent Poor
arxiv-2202-12617.description: Abstract The capacity of a channel can usually be characterized as a maximization of certain entropic quantities. From a practical point of view it is of primary interest to not only compute the capacity value, but also to find the corresponding optimizer, i.e., the capacity-achieving input distribution.

arxiv-2206-07134.title: X-ray spectra of the Fe-L complex III: systematic uncertainties in the atomic data
arxiv-2206-07134.creator: Liyi Gu, Chintan Shah, Junjie Mao, A.J.J. Raassen, Jelle de Plaa, Ciro Pinto, Hiroki Akamatsu, Norbert Werner, Aurora Simionescu, François Mernier, Makoto Sawada, Pranav Mohanty, Pedro Amaro, Ming Feng Gu, F. Scott Porter, José R. Crespo López-Urrutia, Jelle S. Kaastra
arxiv-2206-07134.description: Abstract There has been a growing request from the X-ray astronomy community for a quantitative estimate of systematic uncertainties originating from the atomic data used in plasma codes. Though there have been several studies looking into atomic data uncertainties using theoretical calculations, in general, there is no commonly accepted solution for this task.

arxiv-2403-16812.title: Towards Human-AI Deliberation: Design and Evaluation of LLM-Empowered Deliberative AI for AI-Assisted Decision-Making Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26-May 1
arxiv-2403-16812.creator: Shuai Ma, Qiaoyi Chen, Xinru Wang, Chengbo Zheng, Zhenhui Peng, Ming Yin, Xiaojuan Ma
arxiv-2403-16812.description: Abstract . Traditional AI-assisted decision-making systems often provide fixed recommendations that users must either accept or reject entirely, limiting meaningful interaction—especially in cases of disagreement. To address this, we introduce Human-AI Deliberation , an approach inspired by human deliberation theories that enables dimension-level opinion elicitation, iterative decision updates, and structured discussions between humans and AI.

arxiv-2407-13406.title: Quasi-stratified Order Semantics of Concurrency
arxiv-2407-13406.creator: Maciej Koutny, Łukasz Mikulski
arxiv-2407-13406.description: Abstract In the development of operational semantics of concurrent systems, a key decision concerns the adoption of a suitable notion of execution model, which basically amounts to choosing a class of partial orders according to which events are arranged along the execution line. Typical kinds of such partial orders are the total, stratified and interval orders.

arxiv-2408-05851.title: Maximal Social Welfare Relations on Infinite Populations Satisfying Permutation Invariance
arxiv-2408-05851.creator: Jeremy Goodman, Harvey Lederman
arxiv-2408-05851.description: Abstract We study social welfare relations (SWRs) on an infinite population. Our main result is a new characterization of a utilitarian SWR as the largest SWR (in terms of subset when the weak relation is viewed as a set of pairs) which satisfies Strong Pareto, Permutation Invariance (elsewhere called “Relative Anonymity” and “Isomorphism Invariance”), and a further “Quasi-Independence” axiom.

arxiv-2412-20200.title: Federated Unlearning with Gradient Descent and Conflict Mitigation
arxiv-2412-20200.creator: Zibin Pan, Zhichao Wang, Chi Li, Kaiyan Zheng, Boqi Wang, Xiaoying Tang, Junhua Zhao
arxiv-2412-20200.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zibin Pan, Zhichao Wang, Chi Li, Kaiyan Zheng, Boqi Wang, Xiaoying Tang, Junhua Zhao. Federated Learning (FL) has received much attention in recent years. However, although clients are not required to share their data in FL, the global model itself can implicitly remember clients’ local data. Therefore, it’s necessary to effectively remove the target client’s data from the FL global model to ease the risk of privacy leakage and implement “the right to be forgotten”.

arxiv-2601-21656.title: TabClustPFN: A Prior-Fitted Network for Tabular Data Clustering
arxiv-2601-21656.creator: Tianqi Zhao, Guanyang Wang, Yan Shuo Tan, Qiong Zhang
arxiv-2601-21656.description: Abstract Clustering tabular data is a fundamental yet challenging problem due to heterogeneous feature types, diverse data-generating mechanisms, and the absence of transferable inductive biases across datasets. Prior-fitted networks (PFNs) have recently demonstrated strong generalization in supervised tabular learning by amortizing Bayesian inference under a broad synthetic prior.

pmc-11320915.creator: Xiao-Meng Wang, Wen-Fang Zhong, Yi-Tian Zhang, Jia-Xuan Xiang, Huan Chen, Zhi-Hao Li, Qiao-Qiao Shen, Dong Shen, Wei-Qi Song, Qi Fu, Jian Gao, Zi-Ting Chen, Chuan Li, Jia-Hao Xie, Dan Liu, Yue-Bin Lv, Xiao-Ming Shi, Chen Mao

pmc-11460082.title: Effects of simulated smoke condensate generated from combustion of selected military burn pit contents on human airway epithelial cells
pmc-11460082.creator: Arunava Ghosh, Keith L. Rogers, Samuel C. Gallant, Yong Ho Kim, Julia E. Rager, M. Ian Gilmour, Scott H. Randell, Ilona Jaspers
pmc-11460082.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundExposure to military burn pit smoke during deployment is associated with different respiratory and non-respiratory diseases. However, information linking smoke exposure to human pulmonary health is lacking. This study examined the effects of simulated burn pit smoke condensates on human airway epithelial cells (HAECs) from twelve donors (smokers/non-smokers, biological female/male) cultured at an air-liquid interface and exposed to condensates from three simulated burn pit waste materials (cardboard, plywood, and plastic) incinerated at two combustion conditions: smoldering and flaming.

pmc-11469416.title: Epidemiological analysis of influenza vaccination coverage in Pudong New Area, Shanghai (2013-2023): Implications for influenza vaccination strategies
pmc-11469416.creator: Pengfei Deng, Caoyi Xue, Tian Yang, Bo Zheng, Wenmin Liu, Laibao Yang, Yi Fei
pmc-11469416.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Seasonal influenza remains a significant public health concern globally, with annual vaccinations as the most effectively preventive measure. This study examines influenza vaccination coverage rates across different age groups in Pudong New Area, Shanghai, China, from 2013 to 2023. This study extracted influenza vaccination data from the Shanghai Immunization Planning Information System (SIPIS) of the Center for Disease Control and Prevention Shanghai’s Pudong New Area from 2013 to 2023.

pmc-11675752.title: Prevalence of Vibrio spp. in Seafood from German Supermarkets and Fish Markets
pmc-11675752.creator: Christopher Zeidler, Vanessa Szott, Thomas Alter, Stephan Huehn-Lindenbein, Susanne Fleischmann, Maria Leonor Nunes
pmc-11675752.description: This study investigates the prevalence of Vibrio spp. in seafood from supermarkets and fish markets in Berlin, Germany. A total of 306 seafood samples, including shrimp and mussels, were bought from supermarkets between March 2023 and January 2024. Samples were analysed using the ISO standard method and multiplex PCR to identify V. parahaemolyticus, V. alginolyticus, V. cholerae and V. vulnificus.

pmc-12603589.title: Intersectional Disparities in Digital Health and Mental Health Service Use Among US Youth During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Cross-Sectional Analysis of a National Survey

uslaw-usc-t36-s152306.title: 36 U.S.C. § 152306 — Exclusive right to name, seals, emblems, and badges
uslaw-usc-t36-s152306.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s152306.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 1523 (National Music Council). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The corporation has the exclusive right to use the name “National Music Council” and seals, emblems, and badges the corporation adopts.
